site.tip1: Select 11 starters and keep one substitute per line: goalkeeper, defender, midfielder, forward.
site.tip2: Put players in their natural position; use C for the captain’s armband.
site.tip3: Publish when the lineup is final: players and the website see it, and it locks at kick-off.
site.f442: 4-4-2: balanced and easy to organise. Two strikers up front and two banks of four. A safe default for a mixed squad.
site.f433: 4-3-3: wingers stretch the pitch and one holding midfielder protects the back four. Needs pace out wide.
site.f4231: 4-2-3-1: two holding midfielders give security; one playmaker supports a lone striker. Good against high pressing.
site.f352: 3-5-2: wing-backs give the width with three centre-backs behind them. Needs fit wing-backs who run both ways.
site.f343: 3-4-3: very attacking, three forwards press together. Leaves space behind, so you need quick centre-backs.
site.f532: 5-3-2: compact defence and counter-attacks with two strikers. Good to protect a lead or face a stronger side.
site.f4141: 4-1-4-1: one holding midfielder shields the defence and wide midfielders tuck in. Solid and hard to break down.
site.f451: 4-5-1: crowded midfield to control the centre. The lone striker needs runners behind. Good away from home.
